title: The History of Rockstar Games | From GTA To Red Dead | Gaming History
description: The history of Rockstar Games: founded in 1998 under Take-Two, the Houser brothers, Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, Max Payne and the studios behind them.

sections.heading: The studio behind the biggest games
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are going through the history of Rockstar Games, the publisher behind Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, Max Payne, Bully and more. Few companies in gaming have such a recognizable name. Rockstar does not release games very often, but when it does, the whole industry stops to look. Its open worlds, its detailed cities and its long development cycles have become part of gaming culture. In this video we will look at how the company began, how it grew through acquisitions, which studios do the real work, and which games defined it. Stay until the end, because there is a question for you. Let us start at the very beginning, in the late nineteen nineties.

sections.heading: Founded in 1998
sections.script: Rockstar Games was established in December nineteen ninety eight as a subsidiary of Take-Two Interactive, and its formation was announced in January nineteen ninety nine. Take-Two had picked up assets from BMG Interactive earlier in nineteen ninety eight, and those assets became the base of the new label. The founders are listed as Terry Donovan, Gary Foreman, Jamie King and the brothers Sam Houser and Dan Houser. Sam Houser had worked in the games business at BMG, and the brothers brought a very distinct attitude, inspired by music, film and pop culture. The name Rockstar was chosen to match that style. From day one, the company wanted its games to feel like events, not just products on a shelf.

sections.heading: The first Grand Theft Auto
sections.script: The series that made Rockstar famous started before Rockstar existed. The first Grand Theft Auto came out in nineteen ninety seven. It was developed by DMA Design in Scotland and published by BMG Interactive. It was a top-down game where you drove around cities and completed jobs, and its freedom and humor stood out. When Take-Two acquired BMG's assets, the series came along with them, and Rockstar became its publisher. DMA Design was later brought fully into the Rockstar family and renamed Rockstar North, based in Edinburgh. That studio would go on to build almost every main Grand Theft Auto game. So the roots of the company are actually a mix of an American publishing team and a Scottish development team.

sections.heading: Going 3D with GTA III and Vice City
sections.script: The big turning point was Grand Theft Auto three, which moved the series into a full three dimensional city. For many players it felt like a new kind of game, because you could walk, drive, fly and explore a living world with no loading between streets. It was followed by Vice City in two thousand two, with an eighties Miami style, a famous soundtrack and a talking main character. These games proved that a big open world could be both fun and a cultural event. They also made Rockstar a household name. The series kept evolving with San Andreas, a much bigger map that included a whole state, and the company never stopped pushing what an open world could contain.

sections.heading: A family of studios
sections.script: Rockstar is not one studio. It is a group of them. Rockstar North in Edinburgh makes the Grand Theft Auto series and Manhunt. Rockstar San Diego, a studio founded in nineteen eighty four and acquired in two thousand two, is behind the Red Dead series and Midnight Club. Rockstar Leeds, acquired in two thousand four, developed handheld games such as Liberty City Stories, Vice City Stories and Chinatown Wars. Rockstar New England worked on Bully Scholarship Edition. Rockstar Dundee joined in October twenty twenty after the company acquired Ruffian Games. Rockstar also had studios in places such as Toronto and Vancouver. Together these teams share technology and ideas, which is why a Rockstar game always feels connected to the others.

sections.heading: Max Payne, Bully and other experiments
sections.script: Rockstar is not only Grand Theft Auto. The company published Max Payne, the noir shooter famous for its bullet time action, and later released Max Payne three, developed by Rockstar Vancouver, in twenty twelve. It also made Manhunt, a stealth game, Midnight Club for street racing fans, and Bully, a school-set adventure that let players explore a boarding school and its surroundings. Table tennis game Rockstar Games Presents Table Tennis even showed the label could try something small and quirky. These projects were not always as huge as Grand Theft Auto, but they show how the company likes to take a genre and give it a strong personality, a sharp sense of humor and a lot of detail.

sections.heading: Red Dead Redemption
sections.script: Rockstar's western story began when Rockstar San Diego developed Red Dead Redemption, which brought the studio's open world style to the American frontier in two thousand ten. You played John Marston, a former outlaw trying to protect his family, riding across deserts, towns and mountains. The game was praised for its story, its atmosphere and its sense of place. It proved that Rockstar could take its formula far away from modern cities and still create a memorable world. Players still talk about its ending and its music. Many fans asked for a sequel for years, and the series became one of the most loved in the company's catalog, standing right next to Grand Theft Auto.

sections.heading: Grand Theft Auto V and a record
sections.script: Grand Theft Auto five arrived in September twenty thirteen and became one of the most successful entertainment products ever. Reports said it earned over one billion dollars in just three days. It followed three main characters, Michael, Franklin and Trevor, and later added GTA Online, a multiplayer version that has been updated for years. Take-Two later reported the game had sold over two hundred million copies, making it one of the best-selling video games of all time. Few games stay relevant for more than a decade after release, yet this one is still played and still sells. For Rockstar, it became both a huge success and a very high bar for everything that came next.

sections.heading: Red Dead Redemption 2 and changes
sections.script: Red Dead Redemption two came out in twenty eighteen and followed Arthur Morgan and the Van der Linde gang. It was known for its slow, realistic pace, detailed animals, weather, camps and a huge amount of small interactions. It also sold more than seventy million copies according to later sales reports. In March twenty twenty, Dan Houser left the company, which was a major moment for the people who followed Rockstar's history. The company kept building its open world games with its many studios and new teams, including the arrival of Rockstar Dundee in twenty twenty. Even with leadership changes, the focus on long development, high detail and strong storytelling stayed the same.

sections.heading: Studios, tools and the long road
sections.script: Behind the scenes, Rockstar also grew by sharing technology between its teams. Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Rockstar San Diego and the other studios exchange tools and ideas, which helps different games keep a similar level of polish. In twenty nineteen the company acquired Dhruva Interactive for seven point nine million dollars, according to Wikipedia, showing that it kept adding talent in new places. Development of a main game can take many years, and teams often number in the hundreds. That patience is rare in the industry, and it is part of the reason the company has such a strong reputation. Players may wait a long time, but they expect a lot when a new game finally arrives.

sections.heading: What makes Rockstar different
sections.script: So what makes Rockstar special? It has a few clear habits. It takes a long time, often many years, to finish a main game. It builds worlds that react to the player, with small details like conversations, radio stations and side stories. It mixes satire with serious drama. And it usually releases a game only when it believes the game is ready. This has made each release feel like a big event. Now we want to hear from you. Which Rockstar game is your favorite, and why? Is it Vice City, San Andreas, Red Dead Redemption, or something else? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to the channel for more gaming history videos. Thanks for watching, and see you in the next one.

joke: Rockstar games take so long to make that fans age while waiting, but the horses in Red Dead still look better than me.
